To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in a thermal equilibrium, the average kinetic energy is equal to the average kinetic energy per one oscillator of the environment.

(i) the average kinetic energy per one oscillatory degree of freedom is the same as the average kinetic energy in the free particle case, and (ii) the average kinetic energies in the free particle and Brownian particle cases coincide only in the case when the damping kernel is a constant, i.e., the case of Ohmic dissipation.

the average kinetic (or potential) energy of a Brownian particle in thermal equilibrium state is equal to thermodynamic temperature multiplied by the average kinetic (potential) energy per one degree-of-freedom of the environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
an analysis of a quantum counterpart of a classical equipartition theorem.
the kinetic energy of a free quantum Brownian particle in the thermal equilibrium state.
an analysis of the energy exchange processes between the quantum Brownian particle and its environment in the case when the particle is free.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the average kinetic and potential energies of a free Brownian quantum particle are equal to thermally averaged kinetic and potential energies per one degree of oscillators of environment, averaged over all possible frequencies.

the average kinetic Brownian energy is proportional to the average kinetic energy per one harmonic degree of freedom in the thermostat, averaged over all possible frequencies of the thermostat oscillators, weighted by the frequency distribution.

the average kinetic (or potential) energy of a free Brownian quantum particle in a thermal bath is equal to the average energy per degree of freedom of all the oscillators of the thermal bath, averaged over all possible frequencies of these oscillators, weighted by their probabilities, which are in turn determined by the parameters of the particle-environ- ment interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinetic energy of a quantum Brownic particle in thermal equilibrium is the same as the energy of the particle in a state of thermal equilibrium with the environment.
the average kinetic (as well as potential) energy of a free quantum Brownian particle is the same as that of an oscillator in a thermal bath.

the average kinetic (as well as potential) energy of the free quantum Brownian particle is not only equal to the average kinetic energy (as well as the average potential energy) per one degree of oscillators of environment, but it is also additionally averaged over all frequencies of oscillators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the average kinetic energies of a free quantum Brownian particle and of the oscillators in its environment are equal in the thermal equilibrium.
, in contrast to the classical case, quantum corrections to the equipartition theorem for the free Brownian particle do not vanish in the zero-temperature limit.
the equipartition theorem for a free particle in a quantum Brownian regime holds true, provided the damping kernel is known.
